correctness.rationale: The directed-path criterion forces at most one u_i, one v_j and the common c in a face. Every pair (u_i,v_j) is admissible, whereas the triple (c,u_i,v_j) is admissible precisely for i!=j; i=j forms a directed 3-cycle. These are all possible faces. Each off-diagonal edge has exactly one triangle coface and can be removed with it; the S_m-invariant disjoint pair family leaves edges c-u_i,c-v_i,u_i-v_i. The orbitwise elementary collapses preserve the retained intersection faces, hence give an equivariant strong deformation retraction. Each circle is permuted without reversing orientation: π1=F_m, H1=Z^{m} as permutation lattice, fixed circles equal individually fixed page indices, quotient circles equal page orbits. For m=1 there are no free pairs and already exactly one circle. The all-m argument is combinatorial; independent enumeration verified exact faces/count 2m^2+3m+2 for m=1,2,3,4.
